FACT-1.gloss: Marcy works for the same company for 40 years

FACT-2.gloss: Marcy gets an annual pension of $50,000/year

FACT-3.gloss: After working for 20 years, she becomes entitled to 5% of the value of the pension per year

OP-1.gloss: 30 minus 20 is 10 (years she received the increase, from age 20 to age 30)

RULE-1.gloss: If x is entitled to rate r after m years, x quits after n years, x's pension is p, n minus m equals d, r times p equals inc, and p plus inc equals t, then x's final annual pension is t
RULE-1.formula: ∀x∀m∀n∀r∀p∀d∀inc∀t (EntitledAfterYears(x,m,r) ∧ QuitsAfterYears(x,n) ∧ AnnualPension(x,p) ∧ Difference(n,m,d) ∧ Product(r,p,inc) ∧ Sum(p,inc,t) → FinalAnnualPension(x,t))
RULE-1.verify_reason: It computes d = n − m (years entitled) but never uses it in computing inc; inc should be r × d × p (rate × number of years entitled × pension), not just r × p, so the formula omits a needed multiplication and understates the pension increase.

INF-1.gloss: Marcy's final annual pension is $52,500, from FACT-2, FACT-3, FACT-4, OP-1, OP-2, OP-3, and RULE-1 by Universal Instantiation and Modus Ponens
